title: Rename the stale-approval count so field, code and text agree when there is no current project
description: Filed by the ward-cli worker on 2026-10-26 at the lead ruling that the wording stays for 0.1.0 and changes later, in one piece. DEC-246 (a3) Q1 scopes stale approvals to the current project and reports every other one as a bare count. The implementation names that count in three places, and all three say other projects: the JSON field otherProjectStaleApprovals, the doctor check code other_projects, and the text line stale approvals in other projects: N. That is accurate whenever the checkout declares a project, which is the ordinary case. It stops being accurate when the checkout has no project to compare against: with no manifest, or one that cannot be judged, scope is undefined and every record counts as another project, including this machine own records for this very checkout. The report then says a record is in another project when what it means is that Ward cannot tell whose it is. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THE RELEASE: changing the sentence alone would leave the field name and the code contradicting it, and changing all three changes a machine contract that agents read. Rectifying it is a small, coherent change rather than a release-week edit. SCOPE: pick one vocabulary that is true in both cases, or make the report distinguish the two cases, then change the field, the code and the text together, and update the doctor text fixture that asserts the count line. ADR 0007 bullet A stale approval is named only for the current project and the sentinel test both describe the current wording and must move with it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The JSON field, the doctor check code and the human text line for the stale-approval count all use one vocabulary, and that vocabulary is true both when the checkout declares a project and when it declares none.
The no-project case is distinguishable in the report from the other-projects case, or is shown not to need distinguishing, with the reason recorded.
ADR 0007 and the sentinel test in test/reporting.test.ts describe the new wording, so no document or test still asserts the old one.
A measurement shows the change is presentational only: which records are named and which are counted is identical before and after, and doctor exit codes are unchanged.
